body: Look up at the sky and most commercial aeroplanes you see will be painted predominantly white. Although some airlines use colourful designs, distinctive logos and bold patterns, white remains the most common colour for aircraft around the world, and the choice is not a lack of imagination. There are several practical reasons for it, ranging from reducing heat absorption to making aircraft easier to inspect and maintain.

One of the main reasons is temperature. White surfaces reflect more sunlight than darker colours, helping to reduce the amount of solar energy absorbed by the aircraft and keeping its exterior cooler when parked on the ground or flying in direct sunlight. Dark colours such as black and navy blue absorb more solar radiation and can become significantly hotter, and that additional heat can affect the temperature of the fuselage and the materials used in its construction. Keeping the aircraft cooler can help reduce thermal stress on certain materials and components, particularly those exposed to prolonged sunlight, and can limit the amount of heat transferred into the cabin, potentially reducing demand on air-conditioning systems while the aircraft is on the ground, although a white exterior does not eliminate the need for cooling systems.

White also helps with inspection and upkeep. Aircraft safety depends on regular, detailed inspections, and engineers must look for damage, corrosion, fluid leaks and other faults that could affect airworthiness. A white exterior provides a useful background against which many types of damage and contamination can be identified: oil, hydraulic fluid, soot and other dark substances are often easier to spot on a white surface, and cracks, dents and areas of discolouration may also be more noticeable, depending on location and lighting. White paint does not make every defect visible, and engineers use specialist inspection techniques for problems that cannot be seen with the naked eye. Painting is also an expensive process, requiring stripping, surface preparation and layers of primer and paint in specialist facilities, and fading, discolouration and minor cosmetic imperfections can be less conspicuous on white than on certain darker or more elaborate finishes.

Leasing is another practical factor. Many airlines do not own every aircraft they operate, instead leasing from specialist companies so they can expand or adjust their fleets without purchasing every aeroplane outright. A neutral white exterior makes an aircraft easier to transfer between operators: when a lease ends, the aircraft may need to be repainted in the next airline's colours, and a simple base colour can make that transition more straightforward, while also providing a versatile background for different logos, colours and designs. Bird strikes, lightning strikes and other incidents can leave marks on an aircraft's exterior, and a white surface can make some resulting stains and scorch marks easier to identify, although visibility depends on the type of damage, its location and the surrounding materials, and some cracks and structural defects will not be obvious regardless of colour. Airlines are not required to paint their aircraft white, and many use striking liveries to establish brand identity and stand out from competitors; the choice depends on brand, operating conditions, maintenance requirements and budget.
en.summary: Most commercial aircraft are painted white for practical reasons: white reflects sunlight and helps keep the aircraft cooler, makes stains, leaks and visible damage easier to spot during inspections, and gives leased aircraft a neutral base that is easier to repaint for the next operator.
en.title: Why most airplanes are painted white: heat, inspections and leasing

body: 抬頭看天空就會發現，多數商用客機都以白色為主色，雖然部分航空公司會使用彩色設計、標誌與大膽圖案，白色仍是全球最常見的機身顏色。選擇白色並非缺乏想像力，而是有多項實用理由，從減少吸熱到讓飛機更容易檢查與維護。白色表面比深色更能反射陽光，有助於減少機身吸收的太陽能量，讓飛機在地面停放或在陽光直射下飛行時保持較涼的外表；深色例如黑色與深藍色會吸收較多太陽輻射、變得明顯更熱，額外熱量可能影響機身溫度與材料，較涼的外表則有助於減輕部分材料與零件承受的熱應力，也能限制傳入客艙的熱量，在地面時可能降低空調需求，但仍無法完全取代冷卻系統。

飛航安全仰賴定期且細緻的檢查，工程人員必須尋找損傷、腐蝕、液體滲漏與其他可能影響適航性的問題。白色外表提供了有用的背景，讓油漬、液壓油、煙灰等深色物質較容易被發現，裂縫、凹痕與變色部位也可能因位置與光線條件而較為明顯。不過白色並不能讓所有缺陷都看得見，工程人員仍需使用專業檢查技術來發現肉眼無法看見的問題；對營運大型機隊的航空公司而言，白色讓例行目視檢查較為直接，也有助於縮短飛機停場時間。塗裝本身是昂貴的工程，舊漆可能需要剝除、表面需要處理，再分層上底漆與面漆，並需要專業廠房、熟練技術人員與相當長的時間；白色讓褪色、變色與輕微外觀瑕疵較不顯眼，某些彩色塗料在強烈陽光下可能褪色不均，維持一致外觀因而需要更多注意。

許多航空公司並非擁有營運的每一架飛機，而是向專業租賃公司租用，以便擴充或調整機隊。白色這種中性底色讓飛機在營運商之間轉手時較為方便，租約結束後飛機可能需要重新漆上新航空公司的顏色，單純的底色能讓塗裝轉換較為直接，白色也能作為各家標誌、顏色與設計的通用背景，對可能在服役期間多次更換營運商的飛機而言相當實用。鳥擊與雷擊等事件可能在機身外表留下痕跡，白色表面能讓部分污漬、焦痕與其他可見變化較容易辨識，也有助於地勤人員在例行檢查時注意到某些滲漏或異常沉積物，但可見程度仍取決於損傷類型、位置與周圍材料，有些裂縫與結構缺陷無論機身顏色為何都不會顯而易見。航空公司並非必須把飛機漆成白色，許多業者仍以醒目塗裝建立品牌形象、提高乘客辨識度，塗裝選擇最終取決於品牌、營運條件、維護需求與預算，而白色提供的則是實用性、彈性與視覺簡潔的組合。
zh.summary: 多數商用客機以白色為主色，並非缺乏想像力，而是出於實用考量：白色能反射陽光、幫助降溫，也讓油漬與損傷較容易被發現，同時便於租賃轉手時的重新塗裝。
zh.title: 多數客機為何漆成白色？降溫、檢查與租賃轉手的實用考量
